bottleneck: The blood-brain barrier blocks most systemically delivered gene therapies and editors from reaching neurons at therapeutic levels. AAV9 crosses it but with broad off-target transduction and dose-limiting liver toxicity, forcing a trade-off between brain exposure and systemic harm. LNPs and other non-viral carriers barely cross at all, and focused ultrasound can only open the barrier transiently in small volumes with uncertain safety for repeated use. Neurological diseases therefore face a delivery wall even when the genetic fix is fully known.
current_state: Engineered capsids with better CNS tropism are in development, and shuttle peptides show early promise, but no generally safe, efficient BBB-crossing platform exists. Clinical programs still rely on invasive direct brain injection or intrathecal delivery, both uneven in distribution.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Blood-brain barrier blocks systemic gene therapy to neurons
why_it_blocks: Hundreds of devastating neurological disorders have known genetic causes but no treatment, purely for lack of CNS delivery. This single barrier stands between those diseases and their cures, and cracking it would unlock gene therapy for the brain's entire disease catalog.
